title: The Moon in the Well

full_text:
On the night of the bright full moon, the sky was a dome of deep indigo, cloudless and tranquil. Guru Paramartha and his disciples sat on the ashram veranda, enjoying the cool night breeze.

Feeling thirsty, Matti took a brass bucket and walked to the garden well to draw fresh water. As he leaned over the stone rim and looked down into the dark water, he froze in utter astonishment.

There, shining brightly at the bottom of the deep well, was the round, luminous, silver disc of the full moon, floating serenely upon the water!

Matti did not look up into the sky; he looked only into the well. 'HORROR! CALAMITY!' shrieked the blockhead, dropping his bucket and sprinting back to the veranda. 'Master! Master! The celestial Moon has fallen from the heavens and is drowning in our well!'

The Guru sprang up from his mat, his silver beard bristling with alarm: 'What do you say, Matti? The Moon God is drowning?'

The five disciples and the Guru rushed to the well and peered over the edge.

Sure enough, there lay the glowing silver moon, trembling slightly as ripples stirred the water.

Madayan nodded with grave, cosmic solemnity: 'The celestial orb has lost its heavenly moorings! If the Moon drowns, the universe will be plunged into eternal darkness, tides will cease, and our ashram will be blamed for cosmic homicide! We must rescue the Moon immediately!'

'How shall we fish him out?' asked the Guru.

Asadan suggested: 'We must use an iron hook! We will tie an iron anchor-hook to a strong rope, lower it into the well, snag the Moon by his rim, and haul him back into the sky!'

The disciples fetched a heavy, four-pronged iron grappling hook used for retrieving lost buckets. Tying it securely to a long hemp rope, they lowered it into the depths.

Down sank the heavy iron hook, churning the water and breaking the reflected moon into shimmering silver fragments.

'He struggles!' shouted Peedan. 'The Moon is resisting!'

The hook sank to the bottom and wedged itself firmly beneath a massive, immovable granite slab at the base of the well.

Matti pulled the rope; it did not budge. 'He is hooked!' cheered Matti. 'I have caught the Moon by his collar!'

Guru Paramartha took command: 'All five of you, seize the rope! Pull with all your spiritual might!'

The five disciples gripped the hemp rope in a line, digging their heels into the mud. 'ONE, TWO, THREE, PULL!' they chanted, straining their muscles until their veins bulged.

The heavy iron hook remained firmly wedged beneath the granite slab.

'Pull harder!' shouted the Guru, waving his staff. 'The fate of the cosmos rests upon your shoulders!'

The disciples gave a colossal, superhuman heave. Under the immense strain, the hemp rope snapped near the bottom with a loud crack: SNAP!

With the sudden release of tension, the five disciples tumbled backward in a heap, crashing into Guru Paramartha, sending all six philosophers rolling head-over-heels across the garden, landing in a tangled pile of arms, legs, and bruises!

Lying flat on his back in the grass, bruised and gasping for breath, Guru Paramartha happened to look straight up into the clear night sky.

There, soaring majestically above the coconut palms, was the glorious, shining full moon, completely untouched and radiant!

Pointing his staff toward the heavens, the triumphant Guru shouted with tears of joy: 'REJOICE, MY CHILDREN! REJOICE! Our mighty pull was not in vain! We snapped the rope, but the momentum hurled the Moon back into the sky where he belongs! Behold our handiwork!'

The five bruised disciples looked up, saw the moon in the sky, and broke into ecstatic cheers, dancing around their master, celebrating the night they rescued the universe from eternal darkness!
moral: Mistaking a reflection for reality leads fools to embark on rescue missions that end in bruised bones.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Moon in the Well"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
